title: Manual LRU Cache
prompt:
A fixed-capacity cache should keep recently used entries available and evict the least recently used entry when it fills up. Implement `ManualLRUCache` with the following behavior.

- `ManualLRUCache(capacity)` requires a positive integer capacity.
- `get(key, default=None)` returns the value and promotes an existing key to most-recently-used. A missing key returns `default` and does not change the access order.
- `put(key, value)` inserts or replaces a key and promotes it to most-recently-used. Return `None` when no eviction occurs; otherwise return the evicted `(key, value)` pair. Updating an existing key must not evict another key.
- `remove(key) -> bool` removes a key when present and reports whether it existed.
- `keys_mru_to_lru() -> list` returns keys from most to least recently used.

Keys must be hashable. Values may be arbitrary Python objects. A `get`, `put`, or `remove` on an unhashable key raises an error. Operations should be O(1) average time, excluding the list materialized by `keys_mru_to_lru()`.

Invalid inputs may be rejected with `assert`.

example.input: cache = ManualLRUCache(2); cache.put('a', 1); cache.put('b', 2); cache.get('a'); cache.put('c', 3)
example.reasoning: Reading `a` promotes it, so `b` is the least-recently-used key evicted by the next insertion.

background_note: Two separate xAI candidate accounts support a standard LRU cache with constant-time get/put. The remove and order-inspection methods, return conventions, and validation rules here are local extensions. The inherited Anthropic association remains unverified; these reports add only SpaceX AI evidence.
